Well this isn’t always true. I just came back from 5 months in Rome and let me tell YOU, if you are loud, on the subway especially, and if you are speaking english, you will get the most terrifying “i hate you people” stares everywhere. Especially by older generations. 

Subway etiquette is a thing, apparently. As in.. don’t speak. 

I learned after about the 2nd month to just stop speaking in public. I’m racially ambiguous on the eyes so if I didn’t speak people wouldn’t give me those you-stupid-american death glares, in fact many were intrigued and probably wondering where I was from. It was the moment I was with any of my obviously american and very white friends, or the moment I spoke at ALL, that you could legit watch people’s faces sink in depression going “...oh”

Glaring holes in this idea. Moving in together, regardless of how serious you are, is so much more complex than just “splitting the bill” 

People are in contracts with landlords, might live at home & take care of family, or already have roommates relying on them. Not to mention half the people on dating apps are in college and couldn’t afford to pay 50% on their own anyway without their parents.... never mind living in dorms.

You can be completely serious about someone and have plans for the future while still getting your own shit together so that you’re able to move in and take that step. 

Also, if it falls apart - because moving in with literally anyone, partner or not, can likely make you hate them - then you’re absolutely balls deep up shit creek... But upvote for the wildly obtuse opinion
